Creating a style

Source: vignettes/creating-styles.Rmd
creating-styles.Rmd

A docdesigner style is one file, format.yml, that lists design decisions as tokens: color.accent, typography.base_size, headings.h1.scale, and so on. The engine turns those tokens into LaTeX. You never write LaTeX, and a style cannot break a document: every token is checked against a schema with fixed types, bounds and named steps.

This guide covers the workflow, the rules for setting tokens, the principles that separate a good style from a merely valid one, and closes with the full token reference, generated from the schema itself.

The workflow

  1. Scaffold a style from the existing style nearest to what you want.
  2. Edit only the tokens that differ.
  3. Validate it against the schema.
  4. Render a realistic document and look at the pages.
  5. Repeat 2 to 4. Then share it, as a folder or inside a set.
# 1. A new folder my-brief/ with format.yml, seeded from `policy`.
#    complete = FALSE copies only the tokens policy declares;
#    complete = TRUE (the default) writes every token at its value, as a reference.
designer_new_style("my-brief", from = "policy", path = ".", complete = FALSE)

# 3. Errors must be fixed. Warnings flag risky combinations.
designer_validate_style("my-brief")

# 4. Render any document in the draft by pointing at the folder.
rmarkdown::render("paper.Rmd", output_format = docdesigner::pdf(style = "my-brief"))

Inside a document’s YAML header the same thing reads:

output:
  docdesigner::pdf:
    style: "path/to/my-brief"
    title_layout: page        # optional: override the style's title.layout

For step 4, use a document that looks like your real work: figures, tables of different shapes, a long title, an abstract, footnotes, a block quote and references. The package’s specimen document, examples/gallery-document.Rmd in the source repository, carries all of these and is a good default.

Setting tokens

The format

Keys are flat and dotted, one per line. Comments are encouraged; record why a value was chosen, not what it is.

id: my-brief                 # required; lowercase letters, digits, hyphens
label: "My Brief"            # required; how the style is listed
description: >               # recommended; what it is for and what it imitates
  A two-page policy brief with a sans kicker and a tinted callout.
inherits: policy             # optional; see below

color.accent: "#0B5E55"
typography.base_size: 10.5pt
title.layout: page
callout.style: boxed

Each key appears once. To change a value the scaffold already declares, edit that line; adding the same key again further down is a YAML error.

Six rules

  1. Declare only what differs. Every token has a default. A style that restates defaults freezes them: when the engine’s default improves, your style will not follow.
  2. Hex colours live only under color.*. Everywhere else a token names a colour role: accent, accent2, text, muted, rule, background, code_bg or knockout. Change the palette in one place and every element that uses a role follows. Quote hex values ("#0B5E55"); unquoted, YAML can read some of them as numbers.
  3. Lengths are named steps, not dimensions. quote.indent: md, not quote.indent: 1em. The steps are fixed scales (space, indent, rule weight, gutter, margin, width), so styles stay consistent with one another and cannot produce invalid LaTeX. Margins are the exception: page.margins.* take inches, because a page design needs asymmetric margins.
  4. Sizes are multiples. Heading, title, caption and table sizes are set relative to typography.base_size, so changing the body size rescales the whole hierarchy.
  5. Use inherits for families of styles. inherits: policy starts from policy’s declared tokens and applies yours on top. Chains resolve from the root, and a cycle or missing parent is an error.
  6. Check a token’s status before relying on it. impl tokens render. new tokens validate and are ignored until the engine implements them; designer_validate_style() lists them. deprecated tokens still work and name their replacement.

The validator also applies cross-token rules:

Rule Meaning
indent-and-spacing A style should separate paragraphs by indent OR by vertical space, not both.
dropcap-twocolumn lettrine drop caps are unreliable in two-column bodies.
span-columns-single figure.span_columns has no effect in a single-column body.
markup-no-columns Margin markup (line and paragraph numbers, flags, changebars) needs a single-column page.
margins-override page.margins overrides page.margin; setting both is redundant.
margin-cap No margin wider than 1.25in. The thesis title layout is exempt (college binding margins).
bar-and-rule A heading bar already carries its own edge; a rule on the same level reads as an error.

Structure versus look

Two kinds of decision go into a page, and docdesigner keeps them apart.

Structure is what goes where. title.layout is the main structural token: header sets the title block at the head of the first page, and page gives the title and abstract a page of their own. page.columns (one or two) is the other. Because structure varies by occasion as much as by style, the title layout can also be chosen per document with pdf(title_layout = "page").

Look is everything else: faces, sizes, colours, rules, spacing, and how each element (title, abstract, headings, quotes, callouts, tables, captions, running heads) is treated. Look tokens apply in every layout. A centred small-caps title with a short rule is centred, small-caps and ruled whether it opens page 1 or stands on a title page.

Design the look once and check it in both layouts.

Block elements

Three elements set text apart from the body, and a style should make them distinguishable at a glance.

Element Written as Tokens Use it for
Block quote > text quote.* Someone else’s words
Callout ::: {.callout title="..."} callout.* The author’s own key point
Abstract abstract: in the YAML header title.abstract.* The summary

callout.style takes filled (a tinted panel), ruled (a bar at the left), boxed (a border round a tint) or plain (indented text under a title). If the style’s quotes already carry a left bar, do not give callouts one too: readers will take the two for the same thing. The shipped styles show the pattern. atlantic, economist, modern and nature rule their quotes and fill their callouts; methods, which boxes its abstract, boxes its callouts to match.

Principles of good style

A style passes validation the moment its keys and values are legal. These principles decide whether it is any good. Each comes with the check that tells you whether you have met it.

Measure: 45 to 75 characters per line

Line length governs reading comfort more than any other single choice. Below about 45 characters the eye jumps lines too often; above about 75 it loses its place on the return sweep. Aim for 60 to 72 in a single column and 40 to 55 in each of two.

Estimate it before you render. For a typical book serif, a line holds about

characters≈text width in points0.47×body size in points\text{characters} \approx \frac{\text{text width in points}}{0.47 \times \text{body size in points}}

An 8.5-inch page with 1.85-inch side margins leaves 4.8 inches (346 pt); at 10.5 pt that is about 70 characters. Then count a few full lines on the rendered page.

Wide margins look generous on screen and wasteful in print. If a comfortable measure leaves the margins too wide, raise the body size by half a point, or use two columns, before you shrink the margins.

Leading: open enough to track, tight enough to hold

typography.line_height multiplies LaTeX’s own leading, which is already about 1.2 times the type size. Values from 1.1 to 1.25 suit most text faces. Open the leading as the measure lengthens; tighten it for short lines and large type. Display text (titles, headings, captions, tables, footnotes) keeps its own spacing whatever this token says.

Hierarchy: few signals, used consistently

A reader should be able to tell a section from a subsection without reading the words. Use the fewest signals that achieve it: size, weight, case, colour, rules, numbering. Two or three distinct heading levels are enough for almost any paper.

  • Keep the size steps modest. h1 at 1.3 to 1.5 times the body, h2 at 1.1 to 1.2, h3 at the body size. Large jumps look like a poster.
  • Change one signal per level where possible. If h2 is bold, h3 can be bold italic or small capitals at the same size.
  • Do not repeat a signal for two different jobs. If the accent colour marks headings, a link in the same colour reads as a heading fragment.

Colour: one accent, used sparingly

Most good document designs use near-black text, one grey for secondary material, and a single accent. The accent carries meaning only while it is rare: put it on the title rule, the section numbers or headings, links, and callouts, and nowhere else. A second accent (color.accent2) is for data graphics that need two series, not for decoration.

Check contrast. Body text needs a contrast ratio of at least 4.5 to 1 against the page (WCAG AA), and so does any coloured text a reader must read, such as captions in muted or links in accent. A light grey that looks refined on a screen often fails on paper.

contrast <- function(fg, bg = "#FFFFFF") {
  lum <- function(hex) {
    c <- grDevices::col2rgb(hex)[, 1] / 255
    c <- ifelse(c <= 0.03928, c / 12.92, ((c + 0.055) / 1.055)^2.4)
    sum(c(0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722) * c)
  }
  l <- sort(c(lum(fg), lum(bg)), decreasing = TRUE)
  round((l[1] + 0.05) / (l[2] + 0.05), 1)
}
pal <- designer_style("modern")$color
sapply(pal[c("text", "accent", "muted")], contrast)
#>   text accent  muted 
#>   17.4    9.0    5.3

Paragraphs: indent or space, never both

Separate paragraphs with a first-line indent (paragraph.indent) or with vertical space (paragraph.spacing), not both. Indents suit continuous argument and long reading; space suits reports that a reader scans. The validator warns if you set both.

Tables: let the data carry the structure

Horizontal rules at the top, under the header and at the bottom (table.style: booktabs) suit nearly every research table. Vertical rules and full grids add noise without helping the eye along a row. Set tables slightly smaller than the body (table.size about 0.9) and keep their leading close (table.row_stretch 1.1 to 1.25). Right-align numbers; that is the author’s job (in knitr::kable, align = "lrr"), not the style’s.

Faces: open, legible, and few

Use one family for text and at most one more for contrast, typically a sans for labels, kickers and table headers (typography.label). Never name a proprietary face: a style that imitates a publication uses an open substitute with similar proportions and records the original in description. The bundled families are Source Serif 4, EB Garamond, XITS and Fira Code; a style can ship others under fonts.<Family>.<face>.

Fit the occasion

A style is for a kind of document read by a kind of reader. A journal manuscript under review wants plain structure, a header title, wide spacing (pdf(doublespace = TRUE)) and no ornament. A policy brief wants a kicker, a strong title, a callout for the finding, and a page a busy reader can scan. A long essay wants a book face, indented paragraphs, and quiet headings. Decide who reads the document and how, then choose.

Only the page is evidence

A token can be correct in format.yml, correct in the resolved spec, and still wrong on the page. Look at every page of a realistic render, in both title layouts, before you share a style. In particular check:

  • a two-line title, and a long author line;
  • a table wider than half the measure, in a two-column style;
  • the last page, which often carries only a few references;
  • the first page of the body when title.layout is page.

Sharing a style

The simplest way to share a style is the folder: anyone can render with pdf(style = "path/to/folder"). To ship several styles together, put them in a set: a folder holding set.yml and styles/<id>/format.yml for each style. Fonts a style needs go in styles/<id>/assets/fonts/ or the set’s own assets/fonts/.

# set.yml
id: my-house
title: "My house styles"
version: 1.0.0
format_version: 2
styles: [my-brief, my-paper]

designer_install_set() installs a set from a GitHub repository, and designer_update_sets() refreshes installed sets. A style in an installed set with the same id as a core style takes precedence, with a warning.

Token reference

Every token the engine knows, generated from the schema when this page was built. Allowed gives the legal values: a list of names, a numeric range, a colour role, or a hex colour. Status says whether the engine renders it today.

identity

Token Allowed Default Status Notes
id impl Unique style id. Keys resolution, not the folder name.
label impl Human-readable name.
description impl One line. Note the original typefaces here if imitating a publication.
inherits impl Style id to inherit from. Resolves a full chain, root-first.

page

Token Allowed Default Status Notes
page.papersize letter &#124; a4 letter impl
page.margin narrow &#124; normal &#124; wide normal impl Shorthand for all four sides.
page.margins.top 0.4 to 2 impl Overrides page.margin when set.
page.margins.bottom 0.4 to 2 impl
page.margins.inner 0.4 to 2 impl Binding edge when twoside; else left.
page.margins.outer 0.4 to 3.5 impl Over 1.25in only for a markup style (markup.*), whose outer margin is a workspace for handwritten notes.
page.twoside true &#124; false FALSE impl Mirror margins, alternate running heads.
page.columns 1 &#124; 2 1 impl
page.gutter sm &#124; md &#124; lg impl Space between columns under columns: 2. Unset: LaTeX’s 10pt.
page.column_rule true &#124; false FALSE impl Hairline between columns under columns: 2.

callout

Token Allowed Default Status Notes
callout.style filled &#124; ruled &#124; boxed &#124; plain filled impl filled: tinted panel, no border. ruled: a left bar, no fill. boxed: a border round a tinted panel. plain: indented text with the title, no ornament.
callout.color accent &#124; accent2 &#124; text &#124; muted &#124; rule &#124; background &#124; code_bg &#124; knockout accent impl The bar, border and title colour, and the base of the fill tint.
callout.tint 0 to 40 8 impl Fill strength: percent of callout.color mixed into white. filled and boxed only; 0 = no fill.
callout.rule hairline &#124; thin &#124; medium &#124; thick &#124; heavy thick impl ruled: the bar. boxed: the border, where hairline or thin is usual.
callout.size 0.8 to 1.1 0.95 impl Text size, as a multiple of typography.base_size.

Token Allowed Default Status Notes
header_footer.header.left none &#124; title &#124; runningtitle &#124; author &#124; surname &#124; section &#124; page &#124; folio &#124; stamp none impl
header_footer.header.center none &#124; title &#124; runningtitle &#124; author &#124; surname &#124; section &#124; page &#124; folio &#124; stamp none impl
header_footer.header.right none &#124; title &#124; runningtitle &#124; author &#124; surname &#124; section &#124; page &#124; folio &#124; stamp none impl
header_footer.header.rule true &#124; false FALSE impl
header_footer.header.fill accent &#124; accent2 &#124; text &#124; muted &#124; rule &#124; background &#124; code_bg &#124; knockout impl Fill the running head with a full-bleed colour band spanning the whole paper width, not just the text block. The Economist flag and a government masthead. Suppresses header.rule, which a filled band does not want.
header_footer.header.bleed true &#124; false TRUE impl With header.fill: true runs the band to the paper edges; false keeps it to the text measure, aligned with the body.
header_footer.header.color accent &#124; accent2 &#124; text &#124; muted &#124; rule &#124; background &#124; code_bg &#124; knockout impl Ink used inside the running head. Unset: muted for a plain head, text inside a band. With header.fill set this is the knockout colour – white-on-red is fill: accent, color: knockout.
header_footer.footer.color accent &#124; accent2 &#124; text &#124; muted &#124; rule &#124; background &#124; code_bg &#124; knockout impl Ink used in the running foot. Unset: muted.
header_footer.footer.left none &#124; title &#124; runningtitle &#124; author &#124; surname &#124; section &#124; page &#124; folio &#124; stamp none impl
header_footer.footer.center none &#124; title &#124; runningtitle &#124; author &#124; surname &#124; section &#124; page &#124; folio &#124; stamp none impl
header_footer.footer.right none &#124; title &#124; runningtitle &#124; author &#124; surname &#124; section &#124; page &#124; folio &#124; stamp page impl
header_footer.footer.rule true &#124; false TRUE impl
header_footer.alternate true &#124; false FALSE impl Under page.twoside: mirror the left and right slots on even pages, so right is always the outer edge and left the inner. Slot values: folio is page/pages; stamp is the running title, version and date (see pdf(version = )).
header_footer.section_chars 20 to 120 impl Set: section in a running head shows the first level-1 heading on the page, numbered and cut at this many characters. Unset: LaTeX’s own .
header_footer.page_number.format arabic &#124; roman arabic impl Front-matter page numbers in the thesis layout. roman: i, ii, …; the body starts again at 1.
header_footer.first_page plain &#124; none &#124; header &#124; folio plain impl plain: LaTeX default (centred footer folio, no running head on page 1). none: nothing on page 1. header: carry the running head onto page 1 too. folio: page 1 keeps the band and the folio slots, but drops the running title.

markup.claim_check true &#124; false FALSE impl Flag [[LABEL?]] beside a heading of fewer than four words: a label where a claim belongs. Advisory.
